title: Best AI Support Tools for Shopify Stores
intro: Shopify support has a specific shape: customers ask about order status, live stock, and shipping constantly, and that data changes by the minute, so a tool trained only on a static crawl of your site will confidently give wrong answers about inventory that sold out an hour ago. Chatbase's own documentation is explicit about this limit — it trains primarily on crawled or uploaded static content, so live data like stock levels has to be kept current through re-crawls or wired up via integrations and API rather than assumed to update automatically — and that caveat applies, in some form, to every crawl-based AI chatbot in this category, not just Chatbase. The four tools below handle that gap differently, from native e-commerce integrations that surface order context directly in a conversation to comment-to-DM automation for stores selling through Instagram. Two of the four — Crisp and Chatbase — are tools this site's author has a prior relationship with (contributed content for both), so weigh those two entries as informed but not neutral, evaluated on the same public rubric used throughout this site.

entries.blurb: Tidio is built with e-commerce integrations and sales-assist use cases specifically in mind, and its Lyro AI agent reportedly resolves around 90% of conversations with minimal hallucination — a genuinely strong signal for a Shopify store fielding a high volume of repetitive order and policy questions. The free tier includes real ticketing and email management (50 conversations, 10 seats), not a stripped demo, so a smaller store can run actual support before committing to Starter at $24.17/mo. Where Tidio falls short for some Shopify sellers specifically is channel coverage: it handles web chat, email, Instagram DM, and Facebook Messenger, but has no native WhatsApp or SMS, a real gap if a meaningful share of your customers message you through WhatsApp about their orders rather than the on-site widget. Growth tier ($49.17/mo, up to 2,000 conversations) adds automatic chat assignment and macros, useful once order-status questions are coming in fast enough that routing matters. Lyro AI conversations bill separately from the core plan (from $32.50/mo for 50+ conversations), so total cost estimation takes a bit more math than a single flat number. Best fit for a Shopify store that wants strong AI resolution quality on web and Instagram/Messenger DMs and doesn't need WhatsApp as a core channel.

Crisp's native e-commerce integrations surface order and customer context directly inside a conversation, which is the specific capability that matters most for Shopify's order-status and stock questions — an agent isn't just paraphrasing a policy page, it's pulling real account context into the thread. It bundles WhatsApp and Instagram alongside the core web widget, relevant for Shopify stores that sell through social or field customer messages on WhatsApp rather than exclusively through on-site chat, and starts at $45/mo (Mini, 4 seats) with a usable 2-seat free tier for testing before committing. The AI automation itself runs on a credit pool rather than a flat allowance — $25 of credits, roughly 450 automated conversations, at the $95/mo Essentials tier where the e-commerce integrations and knowledge base actually live — so budget for that tier specifically rather than the cheaper Mini plan if AI-assisted order lookups are the goal. In the interest of full disclosure, this site's author has previously written contributed content for Crisp. One thing worth flagging for an order-status use case specifically: a non-trivial number of independent reviews report message-delivery reliability issues, including one Capterra reviewer describing support replies not reaching customers — worth testing directly before relying on it for time-sensitive shipping updates. Good fit for a Shopify store selling across web, WhatsApp, and Instagram that wants order context inside the conversation rather than a generic FAQ bot.

ManyChat is the pick specifically if your Shopify traffic and support conversations originate on Instagram — comment-to-DM automation turns post, reel, and ad engagement directly into a sales or support conversation, a genuinely differentiated capability none of the other tools here replicate. That makes it less a general-purpose Shopify support tool and more a channel-specific one: its channel list (Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp, SMS, email broadcast) has no native web chat widget, ticketing system, or help-center layer, so it's a poor substitute for handling on-site order-status questions directly. The March 2026 pricing overhaul is the thing to watch closely if you're considering it for a growing store: the free tier dropped from 1,000 contacts to just 25, and per-contact overage fees ($0.10/contact on Essential, down to $0.025/contact on Business) mean a Shopify store with a large engaged Instagram following can see costs scale faster than expected — Reddit threads describe bills growing 2-3x as contact lists expand. AI is included from the $39/mo Pro tier, but it's positioned as an add-on to flow automation rather than a standout conversational AI, so don't expect the same order-status accuracy you'd get from a dedicated AI support agent. Use it specifically for the Instagram-to-sale funnel — comment automation, Story mention triggers, keyword-based DM flows — and pair it with a real support tool for the actual post-purchase order questions.

Chatbase is the fastest tool on this list to get running from an existing Shopify site — point it at your store, crawl the pages, and a working FAQ-style bot embeds in minutes with no code, backed by a 5/5 Ease of Setup score in our scorecard, the top mark of any tool reviewed here. The catch is exactly the static-content problem this use case is built around: Chatbase's own FAQ is explicit that it trains primarily on crawled or uploaded static content, so live data like stock levels needs to be kept current through re-crawls or wired up via integrations and API rather than assumed to update automatically — treat product pages, return policies, and sizing guides as good training material, and order status or live inventory as something to route through an API action instead. Standard tier ($120/mo, 4,000 message credits) is where that becomes practical, adding helpdesk features and native integrations with tools like Stripe and Zendesk that a Shopify store could use to surface real order data rather than crawled guesses. Below Standard, Hobby ($32/mo, 700 credits) is effectively website-widget-only, fine for a small store's FAQ needs but not built for order lookups. Credit-based billing is worth watching at scale, too — a premium-model reply can burn several credits versus one for a standard model, so two Shopify stores on the same plan can see very different effective costs depending on model choice. In the interest of full disclosure, this site's author has previously written contributed content for Chatbase. Good fit for a store with heavy static FAQ content that's willing to wire up live data separately; less convincing as a drop-in order-status bot straight out of the box.
